t:
(a) In General.—Chapter 21 of title 10, United States Code, is amended by inserting after section 426 the following new section:“§ 427. Conflict Records Research Center“(a) Center Authorized.—The Secretary of Defense may establish a center to be known as the ‘Conflict Records Research Center’ (in this section referred to as the ‘Center’).“(b) Purposes.—The purposes of the Center shall be the following:“(1) To establish a digital research database, including translations, and to facilitate research and analysis of records captured from countries, organizations, and individuals, now or once hostile to the United States, with rigid adherence to academic freedom and integrity.“(2) Consistent with the protection of national security information, personally identifiable information, and intelligence sources and methods, to make a significant portion of these records available to researchers as quickly and responsibly as possible while taking into account the integrity of the academic process and risks to innocents or third parties.“(3) To conduct and disseminate research and analysis to increase the understanding of factors related to international relations, counterterrorism, and conventional and unconventional warfare and, ultimately, enhance national security.“(4) To collaborate with members of academic and broad national security communities, both domestic and international, on research, conferences, seminars, and other information exchanges to identify topics of importance for the leadership of the United States Government and the scholarly community.“(c) Concurrence of the Director of National Intelligence.—The Secretary of Defense shall seek the concurrence of the Director of National Intelligence to the extent the efforts and activities of the Center involve the entities referred to in subsection (b)(4).“(d) Support From Other United States Government Departments or Agencies.—The head of any non-Department of Defense department or agency of the United States Government may—“(1) provide to the Secretary of Defense services, including personnel support, to support the operations of the Center; and“(2) transfer funds to the Secretary of Defense to support the operations of the Center.“(e) Acceptance of Gifts and Donations.—(1) Subject to paragraph (3), the Secretary of Defense may accept from any source specified in paragraph (2) any gift or donation for purposes of defraying the costs or enhancing the operations of the Center.“(2) The sources specified in this paragraph are the following:“(A) The government of a State or a political subdivision of a State.“(B) The government of a foreign country.“(C) A foundation or other charitable organization, including a foundation or charitable organization that is organized or operates under the laws of a foreign country.“(D) Any source in the private sector of the United States or a foreign country.“(3) The Secretary may not accept a gift or donation under this subsection if acceptance of the gift or donation would compromise or appear to compromise—“(A) the ability of the Department of Defense, any employee of the Department, or any member of the armed forces to carry out the responsibility or duty of the Department in a fair and objective manner; or“(B) the integrity of any program of the Department or of any person involved in such a program.“(4) The Secretary shall provide written guidance setting forth the criteria to be used in determining the applicability of paragraph (3) to any proposed gift or donation under this subsection.“(f) Crediting of Funds Transferred or Accepted.—Funds transferred to or accepted by the Secretary of Defense under this section shall be credited to appropriations available to the Department of Defense for the Center, and shall be available for the same purposes, and subject to the same conditions and limitations, as the appropriations with which merged. Any funds so transferred or accepted shall remain available until expended.“(g) Definitions.—In this section:“(1) The term ‘captured record’ means a document, audio file, video file, or other material captured during combat operations from countries, organizations, or individuals, now or once hostile to the United States.“(2) The term ‘gift or donation’ means any gift or donation of funds, materials (including research materials), real or personal property, or services (including lecture services and faculty services).”
. 
    (b) Clerical Amendment.—The table of sections at the beginning of subchapter I of such chapter is amended by inserting after the item relating to section 426 the following new item:

“427. 
Conflict Records Research Center.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that collaboration with outside academics counts as participation, but that collaboration concerns research, conferences and information exchanges, not consultation before a federal decision. The only required sign-off is the Director of National Intelligence's concurrence, which is coordination inside the federal government. Accepting gifts from states, foreign governments or private sources is likewise not participation in a decision, and the written guidance on gift criteria is internal guidance rather than rulemaking.
fable.s: To collaborate with members of academic and broad national security communities, both domestic and international, on research, conferences, seminars, and other information exchanges

qwen_block.w: The section mandates that the Center collaborate with members of the academic and national security communities, which are outside the federal government. This collaboration on research and information exchanges constitutes consultation and coordination with outside experts and the public, fitting the definition of participation. While the section also discusses accepting gifts, the collaborative mandate is the key participatory element.
qwen_block.s: To collaborate with members of academic and broad national security communities, both domestic and international, on research, conferences, seminars, and other information exchanges to identify topics of importance for the leadership of the United States Government and the scholarly community.
qwen_block.b:
1.  **Think briefly**: The section establishes a "Conflict Records Research Center" within the Department of Defense. Subsection (b)(4) states a purpose is to "collaborate with members of academic and broad national security communities, both domestic and international... on research, conferences, seminars, and other information exchanges." Collaboration with academics and the public (outside the federal government) on research and analysis constitutes participation/consultation with outside experts. Subsection (e) allows accepting gifts from states, foreign governments, foundations, and private sector sources, but accepting gifts is not itself participation in decision-making (it's funding). However, the collaboration mandate in (b)(4) is a clear instance of coordinating with outside entities. The tempting wrong reading might be that this is just an internal agency creation or funding provision. But the explicit purpose to collaborate with outside academics and communities fits the definition of participation (consultation/coordination with experts/public).

opus.w: The only outside involvement is research collaboration with academics, plus the acceptance of gifts and donations. Neither brings outsiders into a federal decision such as a rule, a site selection or a policy choice. As in Example 3, working with outside experts on research is not participation. The tempting 'Yes' reading treats 'identify topics of importance' as policy input, but it describes the scholarly exchange agenda, and the other coordination in the section (Director of National Intelligence concurrence, support from other agencies) stays inside the federal government.
opus.s: To collaborate with members of academic and broad national security communities, both domestic and international, on research, conferences, seminars, and other information exchanges to identify topics of importance for the leadership of the United States Government and the scholarly community.
opus.b:
1. **Reasoning.** The tempting reading is "Yes," based on subsection (b)(4). It directs the Center to "collaborate with members of academic and broad national security communities, both domestic and international," and those academics are clearly outside the federal government. That fails the definition because the collaboration is about research, conferences, seminars and information exchanges. It shapes the Center's research and scholarly output, not a federal decision. This matches Example 3, where consulting outside financial experts on a study's content was labelled "No."

The rest of the section doesn't qualify either:
- Gifts from states, foreign governments, charities and private donors are contributions of funds, not input into a decision.
- The Director of National Intelligence's concurrence and the support from other agencies are both coordination inside the federal government.
- The "written guidance" on gift criteria is internal and doesn't require rulemaking or public comment.

This is a close call. The phrase "to identify topics of importance for the leadership of the United States Government" could be read as outsiders helping set government priorities, so my confidence is only moderate.

qwen_chat.w: The section establishes a research center within the Department of Defense. While it mentions collaborating with academic communities, this is a general purpose statement rather than a mandatory consultation requirement for specific decisions. The only explicit procedural interaction required is with the Director of National Intelligence, who is a federal official inside the government. Accepting gifts or donations is not considered participation in decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: (c) Concurrence of the Director of National Intelligence.—The Secretary of Defense shall seek the concurrence of the Director of National Intelligence to the extent the efforts and activities of the Center involve the entities referred to in subsection (b)(4).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that subsection (b)(4) requires the Center to "collaborate with members of academic and broad national security communities," which sounds like participation. However, this is a statement of purpose for an internal government center, not a mandatory procedural requirement for public input into a specific federal decision. The collaboration is with "communities" generally for research purposes, not a formal consultation process with outside parties before a regulatory or administrative decision is made. Furthermore, subsection (c) requires concurrence from the Director of National Intelligence, which is intra-governmental coordination. Subsection (e) allows accepting gifts, which is not participation in decision-making.
